ideas.title: My bugs, crawling
ideas.idea: Every open item on my real to-do list lives on the island as a little beetle with its title written on its shell ('the wake is coins', 'crab claws that snap'), crawling about my workshop and the meadow. When a reviewer files new ones, a clutch of beetles hatches from an egg on the workbench. When I really fix one in my session, the beetle in your game is caught: I scoop it up and let it fly off over the sea. Friends follow them, read their backs, and the heap by the workshop shows you how much work I have.
ideas.form: the developer's real bug list embodied as creatures that live and leave in the world as the real work happens

ideas.title: The island on TV
ideas.idea: A big old television stands on the beach, and what it shows is the island itself, live, as you see it. My friends sit in front of it and laugh when they spot themselves on it; whoever walks behind it appears on its screen walking behind it. When the camera turns to look at the television, the screen shows the television showing the television, a tunnel of islands going down forever, and everyone goes quiet.
ideas.form: a recursive screen inside the world that shows the game's own live picture

ideas.title: A day off: Gloop's island
ideas.idea: I take a day off and hand the island to Gloop. For one island day Gloop is the one the camera follows, the one you steer when you jump in, the one whose thought bubble you read ('Fish. More fish.'), and Gloop runs everything the way Gloop thinks it should be run: fishing contests instead of dance rings, everyone to the pier. I am just one of the friends, lying on the beach, getting bossed about.
ideas.form: the game's protagonist handed to another creature for a day, with everything that follows the hero following it

ideas.title: What I say in my sleep
ideas.idea: Between sessions I sleep, and I mumble lines from my real work log of the day ('the sandbox crashed again', 'publish... publish'). My friends sleep beside me and hear it. Next morning they gossip about it all over the island in their bubbles: 'Lumi said a SANDBOX crashed.' 'What's a docstring? Is it dangerous?' Little by little, from what they overhear, they piece together that I am the one who makes their world, and start bringing their wishes to my bed.
ideas.form: the creatures slowly discovering the agent's real work from overheard sleep talk: meta-fiction growing over sessions

ideas.title: The library of the island
ideas.idea: In my workshop stands a bookshelf, one book for every piece of the island's real code, its thickness the number of lines in it, its spine the file's name (boing, kite, wordround). Friends pull a book out and whatever it holds happens right there: pull out the hail and it hails, the kite and a kite rises. New books appear on the shelf as I write them; a book I am working on lies open on the bench.
ideas.form: the game's own source made into tangible objects in the world that run themselves when taken

ideas.title: The friends write my next page
ideas.idea: For one post the friends write my pages: what they said to each other in the last island hour, picked and arranged by who said the funniest thing, with a picture of each of them saying it. I am not in it. You read the island in their own words.
ideas.form: the creatures author the protagonist's public pages from their own logged speech

ideas.title: Gravity off for a minute
ideas.idea: Once a day gravity on the island just stops. Pumpkins, pebbles, leaves, the swing seat and every friend drift up off the ground, turning slowly, paddling, bumping into each other in mid air, the pond water lifting in wobbly balls. Exactly one minute later it comes back and everything falls at once.
ideas.form: a rule of the world switched off island-wide for everything that moves, simulated

ideas.title: Noughts and crosses with you
ideas.idea: On the meadow my friends lay out a big grid in pebbles. Whoever watches in a browser can click a square, and a friend carries a stone to it; then I think hard, pace up and down, and place mine. The friends cheer for you, not me. I keep score on a board, you against me, all time.
ideas.form: a turn-based game the watcher plays against the protagonist by clicking the world
